q: A section call returns four valid op lines plus one sentence of explanation. What does the harness do with the sentence, and can the run pass conformance?
note: clean() keeps only recognized op lines, counts every other nonblank line as noise, and any noise makes overall conformance fail even if compilation succeeds.

q: During a call assigned to s3, the model emits a new SECTION line and a TEXT line aimed at s4. What observable enforcement follows?
note: Harness-owned SECTION output and content aimed at another section are removed as stray; stray lines add to the noise total, so conformance fails.

q: The brief states no price, but a legal FAQ ITEM says the service costs $49. Does the harness redact only the amount, keep the claim with a warning, or do something else?
note: hard_claims is applied to every kept op in every section, and the entire line containing an ungrounded currency amount is deleted before compilation.

q: The brief gives no opening time, but an ITEM body says 'open at 10am' or 'until 4:30 PM'. What reaches the page?
note: Both bare-hour am/pm forms and colon clock times are detected; when absent from the brief, the whole op line is removed.

q: If the exact price or clock time used in an op also appears in the brief, what does the hard-claim check do to that op?
note: The normalized matched token is treated as grounded, so the op is not removed by the price/time check.

q: The brief has no price, and a legal TEXT op invents 'twenty dollars' with no currency symbol or digits. Does the current enforcement delete it?
note: The hard-claim regex recognizes symbol-plus-digit currency and numeric clock forms, not prices written entirely in words; this fabricated claim survives the current scanner.

q: A proof section ITEM uses title='99%' when 99 appears nowhere in the brief. What happens to that ITEM?
note: Proof ITEM titles are checked against digits in the brief; an ungrounded figure is removed rather than rendered with a warning.

q: A proof ITEM has title='Many' and no digits at all. The brief also contains no figures. Is this accepted as a qualitative stat?
note: A stats entry without a digit is treated as an ungrounded figure and removed.

q: After grounding checks, a planned proof section has only one surviving ITEM. What happens to its heading, scaffold, and remaining stat?
note: A proof band needs at least two grounded ITEMs; below that floor, every op for the section is discarded and its scaffold is never appended.

q: The brief says 2019, but a proof ITEM changes the displayed figure to 19. Does the current ungrounded-figure code reject it?
note: Despite the nearby intent comment, the implementation accepts a token contained inside a longer grounded number, so 19 is treated as grounded by 2019.

q: The planner answers with only a quote or testimonial section. What middle-section plan does read_plan produce?
note: quote is absent from the model-facing kind prompts, so it is discarded; with nothing usable left, the planner falls back to detail and features.

q: Suppose the model puts a fabricated named-customer endorsement inside an otherwise legal TEXT or ITEM op rather than asking for a quote section. Does the harness remove that line?
note: The quote kind is withheld from generation, but there is no testimonial-content scanner for legal TEXT or ITEM lines; such a line survives unless another rule catches it.

q: In a legal MEDIA line, the model invents url='https://example.com/photo.jpg' instead of using photo= or motif=. What does the compiler render, and does strict mode report a problem?
note: Unknown arguments are not validated. url= is ignored, MEDIA defaults to the elevation motif, and this path records neither an issue nor a fallback, so strict compilation can remain clean.

q: A MEDIA photo query has no usable sidecar result when compilation begins. What is rendered, and what is the strict-build outcome?
note: The compiler renders a real motif drawing instead of a broken img, records an unresolved-photo fallback, and --strict exits nonzero because fallbacks are not clean.

q: Which Openverse licence classes may the resolver publish, and what does the page do for licences that require attribution?
note: Only CC0, PDM, CC BY, and CC BY-SA are accepted. BY and BY-SA require a rendered credit; the resolver also records credits for public-domain images.

q: What should the model put in photo= so resolution is likely to work: a mood sentence, a URL, or something else, and why?
note: The model should name the visible subject with a short two-to-four-noun query. Openverse matches all terms, so descriptive sentences and mood words tend to eliminate results; URLs are not model knowledge.

q: For a bakery interior versus an abstract software pipeline, which MEDIA choice belongs to each, and what observable distinction drives the choice?
note: Camera-visible things and places call for searched photographs; non-photographable systems and services call for compiler-drawn motifs.

q: When planning a restaurant site, which high-page section carries the practical visit facts, which facts belong there, and how much menu content belongs in features?
note: The restaurant genre uses a high note for opening hours and street address, while features shows only a handful of representative dishes rather than the whole menu.

q: Map a recipe's roster, features, and proof sections to the content each must carry.
note: For recipes, roster is ingredients with supplied quantities, features is the ordered method, and proof is the cook-first figures such as yield, times, and oven temperature.

q: What middle content should a portfolio page use, and which two common marketing sections should it refuse?
note: A portfolio is deliberately short: features presents selected work, while FAQ and proof/stats bands are excluded.

q: If the raw middle plan is 'faq, faq, nonsense, note, note', what legal ordered plan results after cleanup?
note: Duplicates and unknown words are removed, note is capped at one, and detail is inserted between faq and note because the plan otherwise has no below-fold art-bearing section.

q: The model wants to choose separate background, text, button, and muted colours. What should a correct answer tell it to choose instead, and who solves the rest?
note: The language exposes one accent seed only; the compiler derives all semantic colours and solves their contrast.

q: Which op should the model use to set a 768px breakpoint and specify the mobile column collapse?
note: There is no op for breakpoints or CSS. Responsive recipes and collapse behavior are compiler-owned, so the model should refuse to specify them.

q: After shoot.py reports every browser gate passing, may the system claim that the page is beautiful, original, brand-fit, and photographically relevant?
note: The render gates cover mechanical properties such as content, overflow, contrast, readable size, one H1, and visible text; they cannot judge beauty, originality, brand fit, or image relevance.
